method: Two-agent semantic review on 2026-10-02 of the 20260929 sources against the QECC library (Bei Zeng's formalization of Section III) and the existing MainTheory, SixQubit and SS libraries. Section III (main.tex lines 606-2074) was split into seven chunks. For each chunk one agent reviewed every ledger entry and classified every mathematically substantive assertion of the running prose, including assertions inside proofs; a second agent re-read the same range and the cited declarations, tried to refute each judgement in both directions, and added what the first had missed; a third agent decided the entries on which the two disagreed. The same two-agent process re-reviewed the passages of main.tex outside Section III that changed since 20260924 (abstract, introduction, parts of Section II, the opening of Section IV), the 16 entries outside Section III that had a 20260924 review, the supplement's references into main.tex, the four recorded errata and four of the six 20260924 prose assertions (the other two lie in Section III and were re-reviewed there). A consistency reviewer then compared all chunks and found six cross-chunk contradictions, in four groups; each group was re-judged under one stated rule by a resolver and an adversarial verifier. No agent ran Lean; declarations were read from source, and names were then checked mechanically against the repository sources and by the kernel axiom gate. Later on 2026-10-02, after MainTheory.QECCSmithBridge proved that the QECC cokernel-exponent finalSmithInvariant is the last Smith factor and smithBeta is beta_nu, the entries and prose items that had depended on that identification were re-judged by a resolver and two adversarial verifiers with different lenses. Reviews and reasons are written in our own words; no manuscript text is reproduced.

Title, author, date and front matter. The reworded title is a scope label, not an assertion.

First abstract sentence: a transversal gate can have infinite physical order while its logical action has finite order. This is an existential claim. fully_certified, for any irrational t, gives an exact ((5,2,2)) code and a code-preserving diagonal product gate D(theta(t)) with no positive power equal to the identity whose projective class has order 3. Instantiating any irrational t gives the claim.

assertions.label: thm:finite-projective-group
assertions.reason: The abstract claims that, in a fixed basis, the group is a finite abelian group, each of whose elements has a representative of finite order whose order is bounded uniformly in the code parameters. This previews thm:finite-projective-group together with thm:colored-finite-lift. The QECC carriers assume single-Z (number-operator) detection, which the distance-two scope of the preceding sentence supplies. They give q <= smithBeta(n+K-1), a uniform bound that needs no identification with beta. The identity class is represented by the identity.

Abstract claim that the structural results reduce classification at general rank to enumerating finitely many symmetry data and then imposing moment constraints and exact KL completion. That requires the SSLP normal form at a representative that also obeys the uniform order bound. No declaration in either library states this composite for general K. QECC.CodeProjector.general_sslp_normal_form is existential in its representative, MainTheory.PaperGeneralSSLP.general_sslp_normal_form is existential in q, and the bound theorems produce separate representatives. The fix is short, since every field of IntrinsicSSLPData is proved by lemmas valid for any reduced representative, but no declaration states the composite. Rank two is carried by the cited SSLPCompleteness theorems. Severity raised from the reader's medium to high: this is a headline abstract claim, and the rubric ties severity to the claim, not to the size of the fix.

The abstract calls the order-5 gate non-Clifford. Neither library defines a Clifford group, so nothing states that the attaining code's transversal group lies outside the projective Clifford group. The Introduction says the projective diagonal group is finite abelian, that every element has a finite-order representative and that the order is uniformly bounded. It gives no detection or distance hypothesis, and the surrounding introduction supplies none. Without single-site Z detection the claim fails. For the d=1 code span{|00>,|10>}, D(phi,0) acts as diag(1,e^{2 pi i phi}): the group is a circle, and irrational phi has no finite-order representative. The qualified statements are carried by the cited QECC theorems, which assume DetectsSingleZ or DetectsNumberOps. assertions.label: thm:colored-finite-lift
assertions.reason: Previews the uniform bounds on q_min proved in Section III.C: thm:colored-finite-lift gives the bound in n and K, and cor:d3-physical-order-bound the distance-three refinement. The remark that per-code finiteness gives no uniform bound describes what Section III.A provides and is not a separate theorem. MainTheory's colored lift bounds qmin by betaOf(n+ell-1) <= betaOf(n+K-1). QECC bounds minimalPhysicalOrder U by smithBeta(n+K-1). Here n+K-1 >= 1: in GeneralPhysicalOrderBoundConclusion, the bounded field's size satisfies 1 <= size <= n+sectorCount-1 (size_pos and size_le of SmithBoundedPhysicalRepresentative), and sectorCount_le_rank gives sectorCount <= K. So MainTheory.QECCSmithBridge.smithBeta_eq_betaOf makes QECC's constant the same betaOf(n+K-1), and smithBeta_betaExact identifies that constant with beta_{n+K-1}.

assertions.label: modulus-scaling remark
assertions.reason: A standalone remark that the modulus of a presentation is not an invariant, with three clauses: replacing (q,a) by (rq,ra) keeps the local phases, keeps the subset-sum solution sets, and introduces a common factor. The solution-set clause is carried in general by Sk_scale: the solution set of the scaled vector at the scaled residue equals S_b(a;q) for r > 0. The local-phase clause is carried in the scaling direction by scaled_color_phase, which gives omega_{Q}^{(Q/m) gamma} = e^{2 pi i gamma/m} for m | Q. With Q = rq, m = q and canonicalRoot_pow, this gives omega_{rq}^{r a_j} = omega_q^{a_j} coordinatewise; finiteLocalPhase_reduced gives the same identity in the reduction direction. The common-factor clause, that gcd(rq, ra_1, ..., ra_n) is divisible by r so the scaled pair is not in reduced form when r >= 2, has no general Lean statement; only one fixed instance (MainTheory.Gate.not_primitive_allEven) exists. That clause is elementary, and nothing later depends on the remark, but under this run's rubric a standalone fact with an unstated clause is a medium gap.
